\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অন্ধকার} (ôndhôkār)}{অন্ধকার (ôndhôkār)}]{\bn{অন্ধকার} (ôndhôkār) — darkness; dark}

\label{lesson:BN-C505-ondhokar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to rust, then the Bengali for a motor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অন্ধকার}}
\textbf{\bn{অন্ধকার}} — \emph{ôndhôkār} — \textquotedblleft{}darkness; dark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাতে} \bn{গলিটা} \bn{অন্ধকার।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rāte gôliṭā ôndhôkār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The lane is dark at night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অন্ধকার}} (\emph{ôndhôkār}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{andhakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}darkness\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), built on \emph{andha}, \textquotedblleft{}blind\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôndhôkār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôndhôkār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Rāte gôliṭā ôndhôkār.} — The lane is dark at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to rust, then the Bengali for a motor, then say \emph{ôndhôkār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অন্ধকার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Darkness; dark\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উজ্জ্বল} (ujjvôl)}{উজ্জ্বল (ujjvôl)}]{\bn{উজ্জ্বল} (ujjvôl) — bright}

\label{lesson:BN-C505-ujjvol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a motor, then the Bengali for darkness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উজ্জ্বল}}
\textbf{\bn{উজ্জ্বল}} — \emph{ujjvôl} — \textquotedblleft{}bright\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আজ} \bn{চাঁদটা} \bn{উজ্জ্বল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Āj chā̃dṭā ujjvôl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The moon is bright tonight.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উজ্জ্বল}} (\emph{ujjvôl}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{ujjvala}, \textquotedblleft{}blazing up, luminous\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Āj chā̃dṭā ujjvôl.} — The moon is bright tonight.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a motor, then the Bengali for darkness, then say \emph{ujjvôl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঝাড়বাতি} (jhāṛbāti)}{ঝাড়বাতি (jhāṛbāti)}]{\bn{ঝাড়বাতি} (jhāṛbāti) — a chandelier}

\label{lesson:BN-C505-jharbati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for darkness, then the Bengali for bright.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঝাড়বাতি}}
\textbf{\bn{ঝাড়বাতি}} — \emph{jhāṛbāti} — \textquotedblleft{}a chandelier\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{প্রাসাদে} \bn{একটা} \bn{বড়} \bn{ঝাড়বাতি} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Prāsāde ekṭā bôṛo jhāṛbāti āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There's a big chandelier in the palace.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঝাড়বাতি}} (\emph{jhāṛbāti}) joins \bn{ঝাড়}, \textquotedblleft{}a bush, a thicket\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5362), to \bn{বাতি}, \textquotedblleft{}a lamp\textquotedblright{}: a bush of lamps.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhāṛbāti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhāṛbāti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Prāsāde ekṭā bôṛo jhāṛbāti āchhe.} — There's a big chandelier in the palace.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for darkness, then the Bengali for bright, then say \emph{jhāṛbāti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করা} (ṭimṭim kôrā)}{টিমটিম করা (ṭimṭim kôrā)}]{\bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করা} (ṭimṭim kôrā) — to flicker; to glimmer}

\label{lesson:BN-C505-timtim-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for bright, then the Bengali for a chandelier.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ṭimṭim kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to flicker; to glimmer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঘরে} \bn{একটা} \bn{মোমবাতি} \bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ghôre ekṭā mombāti ṭimṭim kôrchhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A candle was flickering in the room.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{বাতি} \bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করল}, \emph{sei bāti ṭimṭim kôrlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{টিমটিম} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ṭimṭim kôrā}) joins \bn{টিমটিম}, an imitative word for a weak, wavering light, to \bn{করা}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}. No dictionary we use records an older form, so its history is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭimṭim kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Ghôre ekṭā mombāti ṭimṭim kôrchhilô.} — A candle was flickering in the room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for bright, then the Bengali for a chandelier, then say \emph{ṭimṭim kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নেভা} (nebhā)}{নেভা (nebhā)}]{\bn{নেভা} (nebhā) — to go out (of a fire); to go out (of a light)}

\label{lesson:BN-C505-nebha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a chandelier, then the Bengali for to flicker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নেভা}}
\textbf{\bn{নেভা}} — \emph{nebhā} — \textquotedblleft{}to go out (of a fire); to go out (of a light)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{হঠাৎ} \bn{বাতাসে} \bn{মোমবাতিটা} \bn{নিভল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hôṭhāt bātāse mombātiṭā nibhlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Suddenly the candle went out in the wind.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{আগুন} \bn{নিভল}, \emph{sei āgun nibhlô}.

The stem vowel rises in the past: \bn{নিভল}, it went out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নেভা}} (\emph{nebhā}) is the plain partner of \bn{নেভানো}, \textquotedblleft{}to put out\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{nirvāyati}, \textquotedblleft{}is extinguished\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7399).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nebhā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nebhā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Hôṭhāt bātāse mombātiṭā nibhlô.} — Suddenly the candle went out in the wind.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a chandelier, then the Bengali for to flicker, then say \emph{nebhā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নেভা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To go out (of a fire); to go out (of a light)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
